Only one task fits in this session. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Call record_choice for the one to keep. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling a smaller version of itself. It breaks a large, complex task down into simpler, identical sub-tasks until it reaches a basic stopping point known as the base case. Once that stopping point is reached, the function works its way back up the chain, combining the small solutions to build the final answer. You can think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where you must open each smaller doll until you reach the smallest solid one before you can put them all back together.
